Results.ReviewText:
The grill quality is excellent and what I expected from Weber and the price point. The assembly was easy for one person to build. There is a lot of packaging making sure nothing is bend or broken. The burners and lighters are very well build. Flareups are uncommon due to the design of the burners and burner shields. Heat distribution is very even across the grill. 

I would prefer that there was a rear wall to the grill base.

The grill is smaller than I am used to, but it is perfect for my family of (3) and can easily cook for a small crowd. 

The grill grates are fine, but they need to be heavier to create better grill marks. There is also a large gap in between the two grates that might loose hot dogs or asparagus while grilling. 

The heat retention is the only real setback for this grill. I purchased in cooler months (60*F ambient) and although the grill easily reaches 500*F when heating up, the heat is all lost as soon as the lid is open. The stainless burner shields are thick and the burners themselves are well designed, but even with the sear setting on, the radiant heat needed to sear and create grill marks just isn’t there. Burgers and salmon look more baked than grilled at times. 

I think during hot 100*F summer days that the heat retention will not be a problem, but I do like to grill year round. 

I am very glad I didn’t save a few dollars buying the two-burner version of this grill.
Results.Title: Well built, but lacks in radiant heat.

Results.ReviewText: As we looked at replacing our 25 year old Weber Genesis, we looked for something with good side shelf space, but with a smaller overall footprint. The Spirit-325 fits the bill. Both side shelves fold down, making it a breeze to store in a small space. The grilling footprint is more than adequate for almost all purposes, and it heats and sears effortlessly. We've even cranked it up with a pizza steel over the grill and made pizza. My only compliant is that although it has igniters for all three burners, I've yet to to master the art of lighting the first burner on one attempt. Still, it always lights, just not as quickly as I would expect.
Results.Title: Excellent Compact Grill

Results.ReviewText: I bought mine at the beginning of last month. Have tried twice to cook burgers on it. The first time was high heat without sear. Burgers did not sear which, of course, changed the flavor. 2nd time, I seared first. Flavor was closer to what I was expecting. The result is obviously to cook with the sear option. The downside is the Sear section is 2 burners out of the 3 which means loss of cooking surface unless you don't mind rotating burgers constantly. The spirit II model provides even cooking results across the whole cooking surface. I called customer service requesting a return and that I would purchase a Spirit II again. Was told I would need to return it to the store I purchased. The store I purchased it from stated for me to contact Weber. Now, I'm stuck with it. I have one for sale...
Results.Title: spirit II cooks better

Happy that I did, but not just for the sear.  Nice to have the extra heat available for grilling large quantities or keeping a high temp on a windy day.

Results.ReviewText:
Very nice, 3 Burner Gas Grill (Spirit, E-325).
Solid Materials, built well in keeping with the Weber Brand, Compact & Perfect for small families. Folding Side Tables are a Plus.

Fairly decent BTU power, and so far the Grill is living up to my expectations, Except For:

*** The 2 Sear Zones are not as powerful as described…. Weber claims the Sear Zone provides 40% more Sear Power - That has not been my experience while using this Grill. A little disappointed with this feature.

*** This Model does not include a Tank Scale…. ?? A nice feature I think Weber should include on all of their Propane Grills. I find it difficult to understand why this upgrade wasn’t included ? The Tank Scale retails to the Public at $40, so Weber’s cost to include this feature would have a minimal impact to their overall Cost of Goods Sold. The Grill itself retails for $500. Not an unreasonable price, but Please Weber throw in the Tank Scale !

Results.ReviewText:
Overall, it’s a good bbq.

 I only didn’t give 5 stars because when I unpacked it to assemble it some of the metal was bent and dented on the left and right side parts (particularly the flange sections where they bolt to other parts) I had to re-bend them back into shape so I could assemble it. 
Also, the center burner igniter consistently misfires for the first 1-2 times when lighting. 

I was a little disappointed with these results as I decided to splurge and pay full price for a Weber after reading about the quality they are known for. 

I like the size of the cooking area and it cooks fairly evenly across the grill so far.
Results.Title: Might wait for a sale if I could do over

Results.ReviewText: It is solid built and logically put together. But it does not hold the temperature at 450 degrees when raise the lid to check/turn the meat or add basting. You can preheat to about 500-550 fair enough, but as soon as you open the lid, the heat temperature dissipates quickly. For some reason the cage/shell metal doesn’t retain enough of the heat. The three burners evenly distribute the heat and I am able to get some sear marks.

Results.ReviewText: I bought a Spirit grill 1 1/2 years ago and it started leaking gas from the hose/fittting.  I called Home Depot and they said they’d give me a new grill. I need a back to the grill so the rain doesn’t get in.  You don’t mix water and grease. I also keep my garden gloves inside the bottom, and they are soaked also.  What happened to the 4 wheels on the grill?

Results.ReviewText: Been a Weber fan for over 30 years. The E 325 is 4th Weber. I like the ignighter on each knob but I fear that may be a maintenance issue in the future as there are now three ignighters vs. one. I like the Sear feature and the overall "look" of the grill. Three major disappointments : 1. My prior Weber's had a metal piece on the rear of the grill that prevented rain from filling the grease pan, but the back is open now so I have to empty the pan whenever it rains. 2. The grates are much more lightweight and don't seem to be of the same quality or hold the heat as well as my last grill. 3. The lift handle gets hot when you cook.
Results.Title: Functional but has some drawbacks

Results.ReviewText: Great product, well built to last multiple season.  Easy to put together . Great heat and controls. The perfect burger, salmon or steak.
